name: sftp
description: An interactive file transfer program over SSH: browse remote directories, upload, and download in a secure FTP-like session.

flags.description: Connect to a specific SSH port.
Run commands from a batch file (non-interactive).
Inside the session: download a file to the local machine.
Inside the session: upload a file to the remote machine.
List remote directory / change remote directory / change local directory.

examples.explanation: Opens an interactive session. The prompt changes to sftp>, and all commands now operate on the remote server.
Inside the session: downloads app.log from the server into the current local directory.
Uploads a whole local directory recursively to the remote web root.
Connects to a non-standard SSH port using a specific key.

about: sftp runs over the SSH connection, so it is encrypted end to end — unlike classic FTP, which sends credentials and data in cleartext. It supports glob patterns (get *.log), resuming with reget/reput, and permissions commands (chmod, chown) on remote files.
useCases: Interactive browsing and transfer on remote servers.
Automated uploads in scripts with -b batch files.
mistakes: Confusing lcd (local change directory) with cd (remote).
Using plain ftp instead of sftp and sending passwords unencrypted.
warnings: Classic ftp and telnet transmit credentials in cleartext; avoid them on any network you do not fully control.
distroNotes: OpenSSH sftp is available everywhere OpenSSH is installed. Many servers disable the legacy FTP daemon entirely and expose only SFTP.
